title: A full bounded queue slows every hop back to the client; an unbounded queue hides the problem until memory runs out
captions: A client sends jobs through an API to a queue with room for 4 jobs. 150 jobs a second arrive, but the worker finishes only 100. The queue is full almost at once.
The queue is full, so each API handler's put() call waits for a free slot. A waiting handler does not take the next request.

Requests now wait in the API's connections, so the client waits too. A client with a fixed number of requests in flight now sends only as fast as the worker finishes. The slow-down travelled back, hop by hop.
Now the queue has no limit. The API adds every job and answers at once, so the client never slows down. The queue grows by 50 jobs every second, and so does memory, until something crashes.
The fix: give every queue a limit. When it is full, either wait, which slows the sender, or reject with 503 and Retry-After, which is load shedding.
